newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tribal repatriation survey begins.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tribal repatriation survey begins.

text.p: An 11-member team of Bangladeshi tribal refugees from northeast India arrived in the Chittagong Hill Tracts on Wednesday to make a survey that could lead to further repatriation, officials said.

Accompanied by three Indian officials, the team was to visit villages in the Khagrachhari and Rangamati districts in the Hill Tracts, where nearly 7,000 tribal refugees who were repatriated in March-April have been resettled.

"If the visitors are satisfied that rehabilitation of refugees went smoothly, according to terms of the repatriation deal, the next phase (of repatriation) will begin next month," one Hill Tracts official said.
"We are confident they will be satisfied," he added.
Some 50,000 tribespeople from the 5,500 square-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts fled to India's northeastern Tripuira state over the past 10 years to escape a separatist tribal insurgency.
About 7,000 of them were repatriated in the first phase, and both sides agreed on the survey before the second phase would begin, officials said.
The insurgency by tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas began in 1973 over their demands for autonomy for the Hill Tracts and the expulsion of some 500,000 Bengali-speaking settlers from the region.
More than 8,500 rebels, security officers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which triggered the mass outflow of tribespeople.
Refugee families on their return to Bangladesh received 15,000 taka ($344) each, free rations for a week, corrugated iron sheets to build homes and money to buy livestock.
Officials said the repatriation process had boosted peace efforts in the Hill Tracts, which border India and Burma.
"A formal peace deal is expected to be initialled between the government and the political wing of the Shanti Bahini in the second half of June," a Hill Tract official said on Monday.
